summary: Teams analyze a business scenario and develop a comprehensive network design proposal for an esports organization expanding to new arenas. The project includes a written report and a presentation, covering network architecture, segmentation, centralized management, security, scalability, streaming integration, and financial analysis. Teams must submit their proposal before the deadline and present their solution to judges, responding to questions and revising their presentation based on an additional scenario element.
time_limits: No more than three (3) minutes setup in presentation room
No more than ten (10) minutes presentation time
No more than ten (10) minutes of judges’ questions
No more than thirty (30) minutes preparation time at state and national level only
submission_requirements: Submit one combined PDF file containing Written Proposal, Works Cited formatted according to the Style & Reference Manual, BPA Release Form(s), and AI Usage and Documentation Form
deadlines: National Deadline: April 1, 2027, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
what_to_bring: Published and/or unpublished non-electronic written reference materials
Laptop/notebook computer (each team contestant may have one laptop)
Paper and supporting equipment (extension cords, etc.)
One single-sided laptop, notebook, or tablet for presentation
competencies: Design, implement, and optimize network solutions, including routing strategies and VPNs, to meet organizational requirements for performance, security, and scalability
Design and document network cable topologies and create detailed network diagrams using industry-standard tools to support communication, troubleshooting, and future planning
Assess end-user requirements, plan resource placement, evaluate centralized or decentralized strategies, and incorporate scalability for future expansion in network designs
Design and implement redundancy and secure remote access solutions to ensure network availability and support distributed workforces
Evaluate project requirements, delegate responsibilities, and analyze technical support structures to ensure effective team collaboration and network maintenance
Apply analytical and problem-solving techniques to resolve complex networking challenges and optimize protocols, infrastructure, and host configurations
Assess organizational risk tolerance and develop multiple technical recommendations for networking scenarios to support informed decision-making
Prepare and present business reports that communicate technical findings, recommendations, and project outcomes to stakeholders
Design and evaluate SD-WAN architectures to improve application performance, enhance network reliability, and support secure connectivity across distributed enterprise environments
Incorporate zero-trust networking principles—including identity-based access, continuous verification, and micro-segmentation—into network designs to strengthen security and limit attack surfaces
Design wireless LAN controller (WLC) architectures and plan access point deployment strategies to ensure scalable, high-performance, and centrally managed wireless networks
Design and integrate cloud networking solutions by evaluating connectivity options, security models, and resource placement to support hybrid, multi-cloud, and cloud-native infrastructures

judging_notes: AI Policy Level 2 Permitted with Citation
Carry-in and setup of equipment must be done solely by the team and must take place within the allotted time for orientation/warm-up
No Internet access will be provided on-site at NLC; however, contestants may provide their own access to be used only for their presentation to the judges
Business Professionals of America assumes no responsibility for hardware/software provided by the Contestant
No equipment, supplies or materials other than those specified for the event will be allowed in the testing area
No personal electronic devices (smart watches, smart glasses, cell phone, etc.) — other than the laptop, notebook, or tablet approved for the presentation.
No previous Business Professionals of America tests (handwritten, photocopied, or keyed) may be taken into the testing area. Violation of this rule will result in disqualification.

At the state and national levels, teams will be given an additional element to the original scenario to address during the presentation. These added elements are specific to the level of competition and are not connected to or carried over from previous competitions
Cell phones may not be used in the preparation room
No advisor contact will be allowed between the time of receiving the additional element and the delivery of the presentation
Only team-prepared graphics may be used in the design. Originality and effectiveness will be given greater consideration
Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
PRESENTATION WILL BE STOPPED AT TEN (10) MINUTES
eligibility_notes: Any secondary or postsecondary division contestant may enter this judged event.
A team will consist of 2-4 contestants.
Teams must be registered for the national competition before the submission deadline and compete in both parts of the event to be ranked.
Entries that do not follow the provided topic or the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Each state is allowed three (3) entries
